qwen-shares-local.json.placement: Requester and both providers were three processes on one trusted Linux x86-64 test host with two cores and four hardware threads.

qwen-shares-three-machine.json.placement: Requester on the Linux test host; provider A on an Apple Silicon machine and provider B on an AMD Linux machine, three different computers on one local network.
qwen-shares-three-machine.json.transport: two SSH pipes with the requester's ordinary host keys; hosts were not pinned by this route
qwen-shares-three-machine.json.timingCaveat: About 370 MB crossed SSH and each provider hashed its coefficient files on first use, which dominates the first step. The providers' code copies are not attested. Not a tuned or clean timing.

qwen-shares-gpu-one-host.json.placement: Requester (CPU) and two GPU provider processes on one AMD Linux host with an integrated GPU, which a separate public inference service was also using.
qwen-shares-gpu-one-host.json.providers: shares_evaluator_gpu.js through a Node WebGPU binding (Vulkan)
qwen-shares-gpu-one-host.json.note: The report's evaluatorTransports field says local-process for both. Source files matched revision d896b678d (deployed from the same tree before it was rebased onto main).

qwen-shares-cpu-fast-host.json.placement: Same host, requester and two CPU provider processes (shares_evaluator.py), run immediately after the GPU run so its file cache was warm.

qwen-shares-gpu-reused-buffers.json.placement: Same AMD Linux host with an integrated GPU (shared with a separate public inference service), requester on CPU and two GPU provider processes reusing persistent workspace buffers.
qwen-shares-gpu-reused-buffers.json.providers: shares_evaluator_gpu.js through a Node WebGPU binding (Vulkan) with persistent workspace buffers

qwen-plain-reference-local.json.placement: Standalone unshared baseline on the same two-core Linux x86-64 test host used as the requester in qwen-shares-local.json and qwen-shares-network-two-gpu.json.
qwen-plain-reference-local.json.transport: none (in-process FP32 PyTorch and 12-bit quantized integer reference)
qwen-plain-reference-local.json.note: Measures floatReferenceExecutionWallMs (2838.06 ms) and clearQuantizedExecutionWallMs (14632.19 ms) with no secret sharing or provider round-trips, establishing the privacy overhead denominator on that requester host.

qwen-shares-network-two-gpu.json.placement: Three separate physical computers over the mesh network: requester on the two-core Linux x86-64 host, provider A on an Apple Silicon macOS machine (Metal WebGPU), and provider B on an AMD Radeon Windows machine (WebGPU).
qwen-shares-network-two-gpu.json.transport: shares-net-ed25519-chacha20poly1305/v1 (Ed25519 provider authentication over pinned distinct-owner enrollment + ephemeral X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 + ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted TCP streams)
qwen-shares-network-two-gpu.json.providers: shares_evaluator_gpu.js through Node WebGPU bindings on both remote GPU hosts
qwen-shares-network-two-gpu.json.note: Distinct enrolled ownerIds (owner-lab-a, owner-lab-b, excluding requester owner-lab-req) and matching shares-manifest.json digests were cryptographically verified per session, while operatorIndependenceAttested was set to false because one human operator controlled all three lab computers.

qwen-shares-flights-separate-fast-host.j.placement: Fast AMD Linux host, requester and two CPU provider processes, grouped flights off (control for the grouped run, same code revision).

qwen-shares-flights-grouped-fast-host.js.placement: Same host and processes, run immediately after the control, with --group-flights (388 flights for 676 projection calls).

comparisonWithRetainedReceipts.notMatched: Different mechanism and guarantee. The homomorphic receipts hide the input from one evaluator under a cryptographic assumption; this route hides it from each of two providers only if they do not collude. Elapsed times are shown side by side, not as a matched benchmark.

limitations: One public four-token fixture, one run per placement; not a latency distribution or a quality result.
No provider misbehaved in these runs, so they show completeness and cost, not detection. Detection is exercised by test_shares.py.

The requester process also loaded the reference model to compare results after the route closed, and computed its own anchors from the public weights; its peak memory therefore says nothing about a requester that holds no weights.
CPU runs used NumPy (shares_evaluator.py) and GPU runs used WebGPU (shares_evaluator_gpu.js); each linear projection is still one synchronous round-trip (169 per decode step).

The providers' coefficient files were hashed against the plan's weight identities by the providers themselves (and shares-manifest.json was bound into the signed network transcript in qwen-shares-network-two-gpu.json); the requester relies on its hidden-probe anchors, which in these runs it computed from the same public weights.

All lab machines had one human operator, so even when distinct enrolled owner identities and Ed25519 keys were enforced (qwen-shares-network-two-gpu.json), operatorIndependenceAttested remained false and the assumption that the two providers do not collude was not exercised.

Earlier revisions and their fixes (0595f8415, d39b135ba), the GPU evaluator and kernel (7566d2142), and the authenticated encrypted network transport (shares_network.js) received independent automated reviews, but no cryptographer has reviewed any version.
The fast-host GPU and CPU runs are single runs on a shared host, so small wall-time differences are indicative only.

Grouped flights were measured on one host only, where a round trip costs almost nothing; a second pair run straight after gave 5.24 s separate and 5.13 s grouped. No network measurement of grouped flights exists yet.
